title: Sprint 1 — Project Foundation & Database Models
description: Set up the Flask application factory and implement relational SQLAlchemy database models for Users and Tasks.

tickets.title: Ticket 1 - Initialize Flask Application & Health Check
tickets.description:
Initialize the Flask application using the application factory pattern (`create_app`). Configure the SQLite database connection and establish a baseline health check endpoint.

### Requirements
1. In `app/__init__.py`, implement `create_app(test_config=None)`.
2. Configure `SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI` pointing to `sqlite:///todo.db` (or test config if provided).
3. Register a health check route `GET /api/health` that returns JSON `{"status": "healthy"}` with HTTP 200 OK.
4. Ensure the application runs from `run.py` on `http://127.0.0.1:5000`.
learning_objectives: Understand the Flask application factory pattern.
Learn how to configure database connection strings in Flask.
Implement and verify basic JSON endpoints and HTTP status codes.
common_mistakes: Returning plain text or HTML instead of JSON.
Hardcoding configuration inside routes instead of using Flask config.

solution.config.py:
import os

class Config:
    SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY', 'yuvro-dev-secret-key-987654321')
    SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI = os.environ.get('DATABASE_URL', 'sqlite:///todo.db')
    SQLALCHEMY_TRACK_MODIFICATIONS = False
    JWT_ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRES_DAYS = 1

class TestConfig(Config):
    TESTING = True
    SQLALCHEMY_DATABASE_URI = 'sqlite:///:memory:'
    SECRET_KEY = 'test-secret-key-32-bytes-long-super-secure'

tickets.title: Ticket 2 - Design and Implement User Model
tickets.description:
Create the `User` model in `app/models.py` using Flask-SQLAlchemy. Ensure passwords are never stored in plain text by implementing password hashing helpers.

### Model Specifications: `users` Table
- `id`: Integer, primary key, auto-incrementing.
- `username`: String (max 80), unique, non-nullable.
- `email`: String (max 120), unique, non-nullable.
- `password_hash`: String (max 255), non-nullable.
- `created_at`: DateTime, defaults to `datetime.utcnow`.

### Helper Methods
- `set_password(password)`: Hashes the plain password using `werkzeug.security.generate_password_hash`.
- `check_password(password)`: Verifies password against `password_hash` using `werkzeug.security.check_password_hash`.
- `to_dict()`: Serializes user info excluding `password_hash`.
learning_objectives: Understand relational ORM modeling using Flask-SQLAlchemy.
Implement secure password hashing using Werkzeug.
Prevent accidental exposure of password hashes in serialization.
common_mistakes: Storing plain text passwords in the database.
hints: Set `nullable=False` and `unique=True` on username and email columns.

tickets.title: Ticket 3 - Design Task Model with User Relationship
tickets.description:
Implement the `Task` model in `app/models.py` and link it to the `User` model via a foreign key relationship.

### Model Specifications: `tasks` Table
- `id`: Integer, primary key, auto-incrementing.
- `user_id`: Integer, foreign key referencing `users.id`, non-nullable.
- `title`: String (max 200), non-nullable.
- `description`: Text, nullable.
- `is_completed`: Boolean, default `False`, non-nullable.
- `created_at`: DateTime, defaults to `datetime.utcnow`.
- `updated_at`: DateTime, defaults to `datetime.utcnow`, updates on modification.

### Helper Methods
- `to_dict()`: Returns a dictionary representation of the task (`id`, `user_id`, `title`, `description`, `is_completed`, `created_at`, `updated_at`).
learning_objectives: Configure foreign key constraints and cascade rules.
Handle timestamp tracking on create and update.

tasks.title: Define `Task` model with foreign key pointing to `users.id`.
Configure relationship and cascade delete between `User` and `Task`.

common_mistakes: Forgetting to set `is_completed` default value to `False`.
hints: Use `db.ForeignKey('users.id', ondelete='CASCADE')` for the foreign key column.

solution.app/models.py:
from datetime import datetime
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash, check_password_hash
from app import db

class User(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'users'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    username = db.Column(db.String(80), unique=True, nullable=False)
    email = db.Column(db.String(120), unique=True, nullable=False)
    password_hash = db.Column(db.String(255), nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)

    tasks = db.relationship('Task', backref='owner', lazy=True, cascade='all, delete-orphan')

    def set_password(self, password):
        self.password_hash = generate_password_hash(password)

    def check_password(self, password):
        return check_password_hash(self.password_hash, password)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'username': self.username,
            'email': self.email,
            'created_at': self.created_at.isoformat() if self.created_at else None
        }

class Task(db.Model):
    __tablename__ = 'tasks'

    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('users.id', ondelete='CASCADE'), nullable=False)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    description = db.Column(db.Text, nullable=True)
    is_completed = db.Column(db.Boolean, default=False, nullable=False)
    created_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow)
    updated_at = db.Column(db.DateTime, default=datetime.utcnow, onupdate=datetime.utcnow)

    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            'id': self.id,
            'user_id': self.user_id,
            'title': self.title,
            'description': self.description,
            'is_completed': self.is_completed,
            'created_at': self.created_at.isoformat() if self.created_at else None,
            'updated_at': self.updated_at.isoformat() if self.updated_at else None
        }
